newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JULY 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JULY 3.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--There may be changes afoot in Greek-Turkish relations with the advent of the Yilmaz administration in Ankara. Following Turkey's unilateral acceptance of a moratorium on exercises in the Aegean, there may be a change in tactics on the Cyprus issue. Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash is due in the Turkish capital tomorrow for consultations with the leadership ahead of his face-to-face talks with the Greek Cypriot side in New York in a week.
--Sir Steven Runciman, Georgian President Edouard Shevardnadze and Dolly Goulandris are the recipients of this year's Onassis Foundation prizes.

--In what some have called a dress rehearsal for forthcoming municipal elections, Athens Mayor Dimitris Avramopoulos was yesterday accused of mismanaging the city's budget. Left Coalition and PASOK deputies said the city would post an 18 billion drachma deficit by the end of the year.

--Unionists and workers are in for a shock when they see proposals by employers' group Federation of Greek Industries' (SEV) 20-point proposals for changes to the job market. SEV wants wage cuts for workers in depressed regions, the introduction of flexible work hours, job sharing, and a two-year exemption from pension contributions for new employees.
--Athens yesterday called on Ankara to extend its moratorium on exercises in the Aegean to three months.
--Pharmacists go into the second day of their 48-hour strike today.
--The development ministry is comparing fuel prices around the country to try to bring non-urban centres into line with price ranges effective there.

--Thousands turned out for the free concert in central Athens by songsmith George Dalaras and his Yugoslav collaborator Goran Bregovic - the man behind the music of Emir Kusturica's 'Day of the Gypsies' - held to drum up support for the Athens 2004 Olympics bid.

--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou is in the wars again over the ministry's plans to privatise part of a National Greek Tourist Organisation beach near Athens. The plan has drawn fire from the environment, town planning and public works ministry.

--The placing of the 200 billion drachma Thessaloniki Metro project with a French consortium and not the lowest bidder by the environment, town planning and public works ministry is undermining the tender process, according to reports.

--There are reports that Cyrus Vance, the UN mediator on the dispute between Athens and Skopje on the former Yugoslav republic's name, will recommend to the UN that the country be formally called "Republic of Macedonia-Skopje".
--Changes to the state pension scheme - currently under discussion by government, unions and employers - will come into effect after 2005, according to reports.

--A modern-day 'Bonnie' will be charged with being an accomplice to robbery after her 'Clyde' was shot by a bank security guard during an attempted robbery in an Athens suburb. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
